summary:
Scope and method. This covers data research only; no project file was touched. Most official licence pages could not be opened directly during this research (network restrictions): gadm.org, naturalearthdata.com, geoboundaries.org, worldbank.org and rug.nl. Each licence was therefore checked through search results that quote the official terms pages. Where possible I also measured data directly from GitHub-hosted copies: Natural Earth GeoJSON and the geoBoundaries gbOpen metadata CSV, saved in wf/ne and .../wf/pages. Re-check every licence on its official page before selling the game.

Map geometry. Natural Earth (v5.1.2, public domain, attribution optional) is the only global admin-0/admin-1 source that is fully safe for a closed-source paid app. Measured: 10m admin-1 has 4,596 polygons, 1,295,319 vertices and is 40.7 MB as GeoJSON. 4,589 units have name_ar and 4,332 have a Wikidata ID. Admin-0 has 258 units and 548k vertices; 50m admin-0 has 99.6k vertices. Populated places has 7,342 entries, all with Arabic names, and 589 of them carry a POP1985 value. The admin-1 layer is very uneven: GBR 232 units, SVN 193, LVA 119, MLT 68, MKD 84, while 37 countries have only one unit. Unit vintages are mixed: Kenya uses its pre-2013 provinces, Crimea and Sevastopol are coded RUS, and some codes are not ISO (SDS, KOS, PSX, SAH, SOL, CYN). So the game needs its own curated province layer (merge and split rules, roughly 2,500-3,000 provinces) with its own stable IDs.

GADM is non-commercial with no redistribution; avoid it. OSM/ODbL data brings share-alike risk for bundled vector geometry; avoid it. geoBoundaries v6 sets the licence per file. Of its 199 ADM1 files, 84 are ODbL and 14 are CC BY-SA. Use it only for chosen files under PD, CC0, CC BY, CC BY 3.0 IGO or dl-de/by. CShapes 2.0 (non-commercial) and historical-basemaps (GPL-3.0) cannot be used.

1985 borders. Most 1985 states can be built by grouping modern units:
- USSR from its 15 successor states, with Crimea reassigned to the Ukrainian SSR
- Yugoslavia, Czechoslovakia, Ethiopia with Eritrea, Sudan with South Sudan (its 10 states map onto the 3 regions of 1985), Somalia with Somaliland
- Indonesia including East Timor; Hong Kong, Macau, the Pacific Trust Territory and the Netherlands Antilles including Aruba

Some cases need a polygon split or a small hand-made polygon:
- Germany: East/West Berlin, because the 2001 borough mergers mixed East and West; also Amt Neuhaus, moved from the East German side to Lower Saxony in 1993.
- Yemen: Dhale governorate straddles the old north-south line, so group the 335 OCHA districts (CC BY 3.0 IGO).
- Walvis Bay: split from Namibian constituency data, which is public domain.
- The four South African bantustans.
- Western Sahara: the 1985 line, since the berm was only finished in April 1987.
- The Aouzou Strip; optionally Bakassi, the Iraq-Saudi Neutral Zone (1981 treaty, registered at the UN only in 1991) and Taba.

Natural Earth's disputed-areas layer, which is public domain, already has Golan, Hala'ib (Sudanese in 1985), West Bank, Gaza, East Jerusalem, Siachen, N. Cyprus, the Cyprus buffer zone and the UK bases. Occupations should be data (an owner/controller flag per province), not new geometry: south Lebanon, northern Chad, Afghanistan, Cambodia.

Statistics. Recommended sources, all commercial-safe:
- UNSD National Accounts Main Aggregates (UNdata terms: free reuse with citation): 1970 onward, covers former states including the USSR and Czechoslovakia, with value added by sector. Best canonical source for 1985 nominal GDP and sector shares.
- Maddison Project 2023 (CC BY 4.0) for real GDP at purchasing-power parity (PPP).
- UN World Population Prospects 2024 (CC BY 3.0 IGO) for population and age structure, summed over successor states.
- World Bank WDI (CC BY 4.0) and Penn World Table 10.01 (CC BY 4.0) for market economies.
- IMF data (special data terms from Oct 2024 allow commercial use with attribution) for government finance and debt.
- US EIA (public domain) for oil, gas and coal; USGS Minerals Yearbook (public domain) for steel: the 1985 world raw-steel total is 789,980 thousand short tons, revised; FAOSTAT (CC BY 4.0 plus FAO terms) for food.
- The Soviet-bloc gap is filled by public-domain CIA publications: the 1985 and 1986 World Factbooks and the Handbook of Economic Statistics.

To spread country totals over provinces, the main tool is GHS-POP R2023A (CC BY 4.0), which has a real 1985 epoch. Supporting sources: HYDE 3.3 (CC BY 4.0) and the Kummu 1990 GDP grid (CC0) as a productivity proxy. DOSE regional GDP could help, but its licence is unconfirmed and it is keyed to GADM.

Military. Avoid SIPRI (commercial use needs permission and a royalty), Correlates of War (no commercial use or redistribution) and the IISS Military Balance (copyright). Use public-domain US government sources instead: the CIA Factbook, DoD Soviet Military Power 1985 and the ACDA WMEAT reports. Model forces as abstract units calibrated to manpower and budget.

Politics. Use Wikidata (CC0) together with the CIA Chiefs of State directory of February 1985 (public domain, data as of 9 Jan 1985). Use UCDP/PRIO armed conflicts (CC BY 4.0, v26.1). Avoid V-Dem (CC BY-SA), Polity5 (permission needed), Archigos (no licence) and COW IGO. Code regime types and bloc memberships yourself and keep the evidence.

Names. Arabic names come from Natural Earth name_ar, then Wikidata labels (CC0), then CLDR (Unicode-3.0, notice required), then manual overrides for 1985 names. GeoNames (CC BY 4.0) supplies city alternate names. Flags: flag-icons (MIT) covers modern flags only; 1985 flags must be redrawn in-house.

Foundation. Build an offline Python pipeline in the repo:
- fetch with checksums, then geometry plus 1985 overrides, then a topology/adjacency check, then terrain statistics
- then population and GDP distribution, then politics and names, then validation tests
- pack to quantized, pre-triangulated binary compressed with LZFSE, so the app does no geometry work at launch
- generate attribution automatically, with a CI licence allowlist that rejects NC, SA and unknown licences

Scenarios are data diffs (owner, controller and claims per stable province ID), so adding 1991 or 2000 later needs no code rework.

items.topic: Map geometry: Natural Earth (primary base)
items.finding: Natural Earth v5.1.2 (NACIS volunteers; github.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector). Licence: public domain. Commercial use and redistribution inside a paid closed-source app: allowed. Attribution: optional ('Made with Natural Earth'). SA: no. NC: no. Covers 1985: no (modern de facto borders). Granularity: country, admin-1 and city points. Formats: SHP, GeoJSON, GPKG. Measured sizes as GeoJSON: 10m admin-1 is 4,596 polygons, 121 fields, 1,295,319 vertices, 40.7 MB. 10m admin-0 is 258 units, 548,471 vertices, 13.3 MB. 50m admin-0 is 242 units, 99,613 vertices, 3.1 MB. name_ar is filled on 4,589 of 4,596 admin-1 units, 258 of 258 admin-0 units and 7,342 of 7,342 populated places. wikidataid is filled on 4,332 admin-1 units. 26 languages are included and FCLASS_* point-of-view fields are present.
items.evidence: https://github.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector/blob/master/LICENSE.md ('All versions of Natural Earth raster + vector map data ... are in the public domain'; 'No permission is needed... Crediting the authors is unnecessary'). Releases: https://github.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector/releases. Counts measured locally from raw GeoJSON in wf/ne

items.topic: Map geometry: Natural Earth admin-1 is uneven and needs a curated game-province layer
items.finding: Units per country are very uneven: GBR 232, SVN 193, LVA 119, PHL 118, UGA 112, ITA 110, FRA 101, RUS 86, MKD 84, TUR 81, AZE 78, THA 77, MLT 68, while 37 countries have exactly one unit. Unit vintages are mixed. Kenya still has its 8 pre-2013 provinces, which happen to suit 1985. India has the post-2019 units including Ladakh. Crimea and Sevastopol are coded RUS, Kosovo has 30 municipalities, and South Sudan's 10 states are coded 'SDS'. Several codes are not ISO: SDS, KOS, PSX, SAH, SOL, CYN. Consequence: ship a curated province layer built from a merge/split table, with project-owned stable IDs (a target of about 2,500-3,000 provinces), rather than raw NE admin-1.
items.evidence: Measured locally with a Python script over ne_10m_admin_1_states_provinces.geojson (wf/scripts/a1.py, a2.py)

items.topic: Map geometry: GADM-derived columns inside Natural Earth admin-1
items.finding: Natural Earth says its public-domain admin-1 layer includes a few columns that depend on GADM. It suggests deleting those 3 columns if licensing is a concern (a gadm_level field is present). The pipeline should keep only the columns the game needs (name, name_ar, iso_3166_2, wikidataid, ne_id) and drop everything else.
items.evidence: Natural Earth forum post 'Licensing: NaturalEarth PD vs GADM license' https://www.naturalearthdata.com/?p=3348 (quoted in search results; the page itself could not be opened during research). The field list was measured locally.

items.topic: Map geometry: Natural Earth disputed and special units useful for 1985
items.finding: ne_10m_admin_0_disputed_areas has 99 features. They include Golan Heights ('Admin. By Israel; Claimed by Syria'), UNDOF Zone, West Bank, Gaza, East Jerusalem, Halayib Triangle ('Admin. by Egypt; Claimed by Sudan'), Bir Tawil, Crimea, W. Sahara, Siachen Glacier, Shebaa Farms, Korean DMZ, Paracel and Spratly. Admin-0 also includes N. Cyprus, the Cyprus UN Buffer Zone, Akrotiri and Dhekelia (UK bases), Baikonur (lease), USNB Guantanamo (lease), Somaliland and Kosovo. A separate layer has 10 Antarctic claims. All are public domain, so most 1985 sovereignty edits are reassignments rather than new geometry.
items.evidence: Measured locally from ne_10m_admin_0_disputed_areas.geojson, ne_10m_admin_0_countries.geojson and ne_10m_admin_0_antarctic_claims.geojson

items.topic: Cities: Natural Earth populated places with 1985 population
items.finding: There are 7,342 places, each with NAME_AR, WIKIDATAID, GEONAMESID, ADM0CAP and POP1950...POP2050 fields. 589 places have POP1985 > 0, for example Tokyo 30,304k, New York 15,827k, Mexico City 14,109k, Sao Paulo 13,395k. Public domain. Admin-0 capitals: 215, all modern, so 1985 capitals such as Bonn, East Berlin and Aden must be edited by hand.

items.topic: Map geometry: geoBoundaries (use only selected files)
items.finding: geoBoundaries v6.0.0 (14 Sep 2023, William & Mary geoLab). The licence is set per boundary file. In the gbOpen metadata (715 files), the 199 ADM1 files break down as: 84 ODbL 1.0 (OSM-derived), 9 CC BY-SA 2.0, 5 CC BY-SA 3.0, 27 public domain, 28 CC BY 4.0, 18 CC BY 3.0 IGO, 7 CC0, and others under national licences (dl-de/by-2.0, OGL, Etalab, swisstopo). gbAuthoritative (UN SALB) is non-commercial; gbHumanitarian terms vary. Useful commercial-safe files for 1985 splits: YEM ADM2 (335 districts, CC BY 3.0 IGO, CSO/OCHA); NAM ADM2 (109 constituencies, public domain, Stanford/NSA 2007); ZAF ADM3/ADM4 (213 municipalities / 4,392 wards, CC BY 3.0 IGO, Municipal Demarcation Board via OCHA); DEU ADM1-3 (dl-de/by-2-0, BKG); NGA ADM2 (CC BY 4.0, GRID3). Avoid YEM/SAU/TCD/EGY/MAR/RUS/UKR ADM1 from geoBoundaries (ODbL) and use Natural Earth for those instead. Format: GeoJSON/TopoJSON/SHP per country.
items.evidence: https://github.com/wmgeolab/geoBoundaries (README: 'open license (CC BY 4.0 / ODbL)', v6.0.0). Metadata CSV downloaded from raw.githubusercontent.com/wmgeolab/geoBoundaries/main/releaseData/geoBoundariesOpen-meta.csv and analysed (wf/scripts/gb.py). The SALB non-commercial status comes from CRAN geobounds documentation.

items.topic: Map geometry: GADM (avoid)
items.finding: GADM is free for academic and other non-commercial use. Redistribution or commercial use is not allowed without prior permission. It cannot be bundled in a paid app. DOSE and many academic sub-national datasets are keyed to GADM GID codes, so use only their numbers, joined by name, never GADM shapes.
items.evidence: GADM licence wording as quoted on the Natural Earth forum (https://www.naturalearthdata.com/?p=3348) and OSM legal-talk (https://lists.openstreetmap.org/pipermail/legal-talk/2015-August/008178.html). gadm.org/license.html itself could not be opened during research.

items.topic: Map geometry: OSM-derived data, ODbL (avoid for shipped geometry)
items.finding: Under ODbL a produced work (a rendered map) may carry any licence, but a derivative database must be share-alike. Recipients of a produced work can request the derivative database used to make it. Bundled vector geometry that can be extracted may be judged a database; a court would decide. Attribution is mandatory. Decision: do not ship OSM-derived polygons, including the berm line or any of the 84 ODbL ADM1 files in geoBoundaries.

items.topic: 1985 borders: historical-border datasets (avoid)
items.finding: CShapes 2.0 (ETH Zurich/PRIO, state and dependency borders 1886-2019) is non-commercial. The ETH Research Collection lists CC BY-NC 4.0 and another catalogue lists CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so it is unusable. aourednik/historical-basemaps is GPL-3.0 and self-described as work in progress, so it cannot go in a closed-source app. Both may be looked at privately to sanity-check own-work polygons, but nothing may be copied.

items.topic: Terrain: elevation
items.finding: GMTED2010 (USGS/NGA; 7.5, 15 and 30 arc-second): access constraints 'No restrictions'; USGS data is public domain and credit is requested. Commercial use and redistribution allowed; no SA or NC. ETOPO 2022 (NOAA NCEI; 15, 30 and 60 arc-second; DOI 10.25921/fd45-gt74) is a US federal work. Its metadata says it is available to the public, but an explicit licence line was not seen. Use either one offline to compute per-province mean elevation and ruggedness, and ship only those statistics plus an optional low-resolution hillshade texture. Both rasters are hundreds of MB or more and are never bundled raw.
items.evidence: https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/USGS_GMTED2010_FULL ; UNEP/GRID metadata record for GMTED2010 ; https://doi.org/10.25921/Fd45-Gt74

items.topic: Terrain: land cover and terrain classes
items.finding: ESA WorldCover 10 m 2020/2021 (ESA/VITO): CC BY 4.0, commercial use allowed with attribution. Covers 1985: no (2020-21). Natural Earth geography_regions_polys: 1,047 public-domain polygons, including 222 mountain ranges, 72 plateaus, 58 deserts, 30 plains, 12 deltas, 4 tundra and 3 wetlands. ESA CCI Land Cover 300 m (1992-2020/22) is the closest in time to 1985, but its licence was not verified. Derive per-province fractions (forest, mountain, desert, marsh, urban) offline and ship only numbers.

items.topic: Terrain: rivers, lakes and coast
items.finding: Natural Earth rivers_lake_centerlines: 1,455 features, 256k vertices, 7.3 MB. Lakes: 1,355 features, 5.0 MB. Plus coastline and land layers. All public domain, used for river-crossing penalties on province adjacency edges and for map drawing. HydroSHEDS is described in catalogues as free for commercial and non-commercial use under its own licence agreement (some catalogues say CC BY 4.0), but that was not verified on the official page. It is not needed.

items.topic: 1985 borders: entities built only by grouping modern admin-0 and admin-1 units
items.finding: USSR = the 15 successor admin-0 units plus the Baikonur lease. Reassign NE's RUS-coded Crimea and Sevastopol to the Ukrainian SSR; Abkhazia, South Ossetia, Transnistria and Nagorno-Karabakh sit inside their SSRs. SFR Yugoslavia = SVN, HRV, BIH, SRB, MNE, MKD, with KOS as SAP Kosovo of Serbia (merge NE's 193 SVN, 84 MKD and 30 KOS units). Czechoslovakia = CZE + SVK. Ethiopia = ETH + ERI (Eritrea independent 24/25 May 1993). Sudan = SDN + NE 'SDS' (South Sudan independent 9 Jul 2011); the 10 SDS states group into the 3 regions of 1985: Bahr al-Ghazal, Equatoria, Upper Nile. Somalia = SOM + SOL. Indonesia includes Timor-Leste (independent 20 May 2002). British Hong Kong = HKG (Joint Declaration in force 27 May 1985; handover 1997). Portuguese Macau = MAC (to 1999). US Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands = FSM + MHL + PLW + MNP (RMI compact effective 21 Oct 1986; FSM and NMI 3 Nov 1986; Palau's trusteeship ended 1994). Netherlands Antilles = Aruba + Curacao + Sint Maarten + BES (Aruba separated 1 Jan 1986; Antilles dissolved 10 Oct 2010). Saint-Martin and Saint-Barthelemy belong under Guadeloupe. Cyprus: keep N. Cyprus (declared 1983, recognised only by Turkey), the UN buffer zone and the UK bases. Brunei (independent 1 Jan 1984) and Saint Kitts and Nevis (19 Sep 1983) are already sovereign, so no change.
items.evidence: Brunei: https://history.state.gov/countries/brunei. St Kitts: GATT notice https://www.wto.org/gatt_docs/English/SULPDF/91010161.pdf. Compacts: https://www.reaganlibrary.gov/research/speeches/110386a and UNSC res. 683 https://www.refworld.org/legal/resolution/unsc/1990/en/88167. Aruba: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Status_aparte. Hong Kong JD: https://www.yearbook.gov.hk/1997/ch2/e2c.htm. Yemen, Eritrea, South Sudan, Timor dates: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yemeni_unification and the US State Dept nationality notes. NE codes measured locally.

items.topic: 1985 borders: Germany needs two polygon splits
items.finding: GDR = Brandenburg, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Sachsen, Sachsen-Anhalt, Thueringen and East Berlin. FRG = the other 10 Laender plus West Berlin, which was under Allied status. Split 1: Berlin is a single NE unit, and the 1 Jan 2001 reform merged 23 boroughs into 12. Mitte (Mitte + Tiergarten + Wedding) and Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg each combine East and West parts, so modern boroughs cannot simply be grouped. Draw the 1985 sector line as a simplified own-work polyline (tens of vertices) from public-domain maps, or derive it from BKG/Berlin data under dl-de/by-2-0. Split 2: Amt Neuhaus, on the right bank of the Elbe, was in the GDR and moved to Lower Saxony in 1993. Take the municipal polygon from BKG VG250 (dl-de/by-2-0, commercial use with attribution) or ignore it at game scale.
items.evidence: Berlin reform: https://www.entwicklungsstadt.de/berlin-neu-geordnet-die-bezirksreform-von-2001-und-ihre-folgen/ and https://simple.wikipedia.com/wiki/Boroughs_of_Berlin. Amt Neuhaus: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amt_Neuhaus. geoBoundaries DEU licence dl-de/by-2-0 from the metadata CSV.

items.topic: 1985 borders: North Yemen (YAR) and South Yemen (PDRY)
items.finding: The two states unified on 22 May 1990. Modern governorates straddle the old line; for example Dhale governorate has 9 districts, 5 from the South and 4 from the North. Rebuild the line by grouping the 335 CSO/OCHA districts (geoBoundaries YEM ADM2, CC BY 3.0 IGO per metadata; re-check on HDX). Keep Natural Earth admin-1 (public domain) elsewhere, because geoBoundaries YEM ADM1 is ODbL. The eastern line was undemarcated in 1985, and the modern Saudi-Yemen (2000) and Oman-Yemen (1992) borders differ only in empty desert, which is acceptable.
items.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhale_Governorate (5 South + 4 North districts) ; geoBoundaries metadata CSV ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yemeni_unification

items.topic: 1985 borders: Namibia and Walvis Bay
items.finding: South West Africa was under South African administration until independence on 21 Mar 1990. Walvis Bay and the Penguin Islands stayed South African until the treaty took effect on 1 Mar 1994. Geometry: Namibia is a Natural Earth admin-0 unit; split Walvis Bay out of Erongo using Namibia ADM2 constituencies (geoBoundaries NAM ADM2, public domain, Stanford/Namibia Statistics Agency 2007). In 1985 it was a South African exclave attached to the Cape Province.

items.topic: 1985 borders: South African bantustans (TBVC)
items.finding: Transkei (26 Oct 1976), Bophuthatswana (6 Dec 1977), Venda (13 Sep 1979) and Ciskei (4 Dec 1981) were nominally independent and recognised only by South Africa. They were reincorporated on 27 Apr 1994. Bophuthatswana was split into several separate pieces. They cannot be built from modern provinces, which cut across them. Option A (recommended): hand-digitise simplified polygons from public-domain US-government maps of the 1980s, as own work. Option B: approximate them by grouping ZAF wards or local municipalities (geoBoundaries ZAF ADM4 with 4,392 wards or ADM3 with 213 municipalities, CC BY 3.0 IGO). Model them as South African client states; the self-governing homelands are optional.

items.topic: 1985 borders: Western Sahara
items.finding: Natural Earth has one SAH unit ('Indeterminate'). Mauritania had left in 1979, and Morocco controlled the area behind its berm system. The berm was built in stages from 1980/81; the sixth and last section was finished in April 1987, so the area Morocco held on 1 Jan 1985 was smaller than today. The split (Moroccan-held vs Polisario/SADR zone) must be own-digitised from public-domain period maps. Do not use OSM berm geometry. Morocco walked out of the OAU on 12 Nov 1984 over the SADR's admission.

items.topic: 1985 borders: Israel and occupied territories, Sinai, Lebanon
items.finding: Sinai was returned on 25 Apr 1982, except Taba (about 1 km2), which Israel held until 15 Mar 1989 after the 1988 arbitration. Golan: Israeli law applied in 1981 (NE disputed polygon 'Golan Heights' plus the UNDOF zone). West Bank and Gaza were Israeli-occupied (NE PSX admin-1 units 'West Bank' and 'Gaza Strip'); Jordan's claim lasted until its 1988 disengagement. East Jerusalem is an NE disputed polygon. South Lebanon: on 1 Jan 1985 the IDF was still deep in Lebanon; it withdrew in phases from February 1985 and by 10 June 1985 held a self-declared 'security zone' (about 10% of Lebanon) with the SLA until May 2000. Model this as province controller flags plus scripted events, not as geometry; the same applies to Syrian forces in Lebanon.
items.evidence: Sinai: https://www.csmonitor.com/1982/0426/042647.html. Taba: https://www.encyclopedia.com/history/asia-and-africa/middle-eastern-history/taba. Lebanon: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Lebanon_conflict_(1985%E2%80%932000) and CRS RS20566. NE features measured locally.

items.topic: 1985 borders: Chad/Libya (Aouzou Strip)
items.finding: Libya occupied the Aouzou Strip until the ICJ ruled for Chad in 1994 (16 votes to 1); UNASOG monitored the Libyan withdrawal from May to June 1994. Modern Chad admin-1 units (Tibesti, Borkou, Ennedi) cut across the strip, so it needs an own polygon built from the treaty's straight lines (a few vertices). In 1985 much of northern Chad was also held by the Libyan-backed GUNT; model that with controller flags.

items.topic: 1985 borders: Iraq-Saudi and Saudi-Kuwait neutral zones
items.finding: Iraq-Saudi: the partition treaty was signed in Baghdad on 26 Dec 1981 and approved by Iraq's assembly in Jan 1982, but registered with the UN only on 1 Jun 1991 (UNTS vol. 1638). The US Geographer (1992) treats the 1981 line as the boundary. For 1985, either use the modern line (no work) or draw the diamond-shaped zone as a jointly held own polygon from the treaty coordinates. Saudi-Kuwait: the partition agreement of 7 Jul 1965 took effect on 25 Jul 1966 and demarcation took effect in 1969/70; oil stayed shared 50/50. No geometry change; model the shared oil revenue.

items.topic: 1985 borders: Hala'ib, Bakassi and other small cases
items.finding: Hala'ib: under joint or Sudanese administration until 1992; Egypt took control in stages between 1992 and 1995. In 1985, assign NE's 'Halayib Triangle' polygon to Sudan; Bir Tawil is unclaimed. Bakassi: Nigerian-controlled in 1985; after the ICJ ruling in 2002, authority passed to Cameroon on 14 Aug 2008. It is optional at game scale and would be a small own-work polygon (Cameroon ADM3 in geoBoundaries is ODbL). Siachen: India has held it since 1984 (NE unit KAS).

items.topic: 1985 scenario: status changes during 1985-86 (event data)
items.finding: 1 Feb 1985: Greenland leaves the EEC. 27 May 1985: the Sino-British Joint Declaration enters into force. 11 Jun 1985: Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon becomes a territorial collectivity. 3 Oct 1985: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands are separated from the Falkland Islands Dependencies (SI 1985/449). 1 Jan 1986: Spain and Portugal join the EC (from 10 to 12 members) and Aruba separates from the Netherlands Antilles. Oct-Nov 1986: the Marshall Islands and FSM compacts take effect. These should be scripted historical events, not starting borders.

items.topic: Statistics: UNSD National Accounts, Analysis of Main Aggregates (AMA)
items.finding: Publisher: UN Statistics Division. A complete and consistent set of series from 1970 onward: GDP by expenditure, gross value added by kind of activity (agriculture, industry, manufacturing, services), GNI and per-capita figures. It includes former entities such as 'Former USSR' and 'Former Czechoslovakia' (UNdata shows Former USSR per-capita GDP in 1985 at 3,290 current USD). Terms (UNdata): free of charge; may be copied, duplicated and redistributed provided UNdata is cited, so commercial use is allowed with attribution; no SA or NC. Granularity: country. Format: CSV/API. This is the best single canonical source for 1985 nominal USD GDP and sector shares for every 1985 state.

items.topic: Statistics: Maddison Project Database 2023
items.finding: Publisher: GGDC, University of Groningen (Bolt and van Zanden). Licence: CC BY 4.0; commercial use and redistribution allowed with attribution; no SA or NC. Covers 1985: yes. 169 countries up to 2022; real GDP per capita (2011 international dollars) and population. Granularity: country. Format: Excel/Stata via Dataverse DOI 10.34894/INZBF2, a few MB. Extra rule: cite the original papers when the data is shown graphically or when fewer than 12 countries are used. Czechoslovakia and Yugoslavia have non-ISO codes (R package docs). OWID notes that series for former countries are estimated.

items.topic: Statistics: World Bank WDI and Penn World Table
items.finding: WDI: World Bank default licence CC BY 4.0 unless otherwise specified; some third-party-sourced series carry other terms. Commercial use allowed with attribution; CSV/API bulk download of about 200 MB (approximate). PWT 10.01: GGDC, CC BY 4.0, 183 countries 1950-2019 (released 23 Jan 2023), country level, capital stock, employment and TFP. Both cover today's economies, so they are good for 1985 market economies but weak for the Soviet bloc.

items.topic: Statistics: UN World Population Prospects 2024
items.finding: Publisher: UN DESA Population Division. Licence: CC BY 3.0 IGO; commercial use allowed with attribution; no SA or NC. Covers 1985: yes, as estimates for current countries 1950-2100. Granularity: country, by age and sex. Format: CSV/XLSX, tens to hundreds of MB. Sum successor states to get 1985 totals for the USSR, Yugoslavia, Czechoslovakia and so on; males aged 15-49 drive manpower. East and West Germany need a separate split (Laender shares or CIA figures).

items.topic: Statistics: IMF data terms
items.finding: The current IMF terms (version effective 11 Oct 2024) contain special data terms. Despite the general ban on commercial use of IMF content, users may download, extract, copy, create derivative works, publish, distribute and use IMF statistical data, provided they credit 'Source: International Monetary Fund, <database>'. Third-party data inside IMF products may have separate terms. Use the World Economic Outlook (1980 onward), Government Finance Statistics and the Historical Public Debt Database for 1985 revenue, spending and debt where available.

items.topic: Statistics: energy (oil, gas, coal)
items.finding: US EIA International Energy Statistics: most series run from 1980 (production, consumption, trade, reserves; oil, gas, coal, electricity). As a US government publication it is public domain; EIA asks for credit like 'Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration (date)'. Commercial use and redistribution allowed; no SA or NC; country level; CSV/API. Do not use the EIA logo. Soviet-bloc detail: the CIA 'International Energy Statistical Review' (1980s issues, CIA reading room, public domain). The Energy Institute Statistical Review (formerly BP, from 1965) is free to access, but no reuse licence was found, so avoid it.

items.topic: Statistics: steel
items.finding: USGS Minerals Yearbook, 'Iron and Steel' chapter (USGS federal work, public domain under 17 USC 105). The 1986 edition has a world raw-steel table by country for 1981-1985: the 1985 world total is 788,119 thousand short tons (preliminary), revised to 789,980 in the 1987 edition. There are also country chapters, such as 'The Mineral Industry of the U.S.S.R.'. Country level; scanned text (UW-Madison digital collection).

items.topic: Statistics: food and agriculture (FAOSTAT)
items.finding: Publisher: FAO. Licence: CC BY 4.0 by default for FAO corporate statistical databases (since 30 Nov 2019; 2025 policy), plus FAO's additional terms of use, which include 'prohibited uses'; read these before release. Commercial use is presumed allowed with attribution; no SA or NC. Covers 1985: yes (1961 onward). Country level, crop and livestock production. Historical areas exist (USSR etc.), but the exact codes were not verified. Format: CSV bulk, hundreds of MB.

items.topic: Statistics: Soviet-bloc gap filled with CIA public-domain publications
items.finding: CIA World Factbook: the CIA states it is public domain and 'may be copied freely without permission'; the CIA seal is excluded. The 1985 edition (CR WF 85-001, May 1985) is in the CIA FOIA reading room; the 1986 edition is on DTIC (AD1136372). Use these or Gutenberg copies. Avoid the Oxford Text Archive 1990 text, which is relabelled CC BY-NC-SA. The CIA Handbook of Economic Statistics (1986 and 1987 editions in the reading room) gives CIA GNP estimates for the USSR and Eastern Europe in comparable dollars. Country level; PDF/OCR, so manual transcription with QA is needed.

items.topic: Province distribution: GHS-POP R2023A (has a true 1985 epoch)
items.finding: Publisher: European Commission JRC. Population grids for 1975-2030 every 5 years, including 1985, at 100 m and 1 km (Mollweide, plus WGS84 versions). Licence: CC BY 4.0 / 'reuse is authorised, provided the source is acknowledged'. Commercial use allowed; no SA or NC. DOI 10.2905/2FF68A52-5B5B-4A22-8F40-C41DA8332CFE. GeoTIFF; the 1 km global epoch is roughly hundreds of MB. Sum the grid within each province polygon and scale to UN WPP country totals.

items.topic: Province distribution: HYDE 3.3
items.finding: Publisher: Utrecht University / PBL. Licence: CC BY 4.0; commercial use allowed with attribution. Coverage 10,000 BCE to 2023 CE. 5 arc-minute grids of total, urban and rural population, density, built-up area and land use (cropland, pasture), ESRI ASCII format. HYDE 3.4 has since replaced it. Use as a cross-check and for agricultural land shares around 1985.

items.topic: Province distribution: gridded and sub-national GDP
items.finding: Kummu, Taka and Guillaume (2018): gridded GDP per capita (PPP), total GDP and HDI for 1990-2015 at 5 arc-minute, plus 30 arc-second GDP for 1990, 2000 and 2015. Dryad doi:10.5061/dryad.dk1j0, CC0 according to university mirrors; the 2025 update (1990-2022) is CC BY. Use the 1990 layer as a relative-productivity proxy for 1985 province GDP shares. DOSE (MCC/PIK, Wenz et al. 2023): 1,661 regions in 83 countries, 1960 (or 1953) to 2020, regional output in local currency and USD, keyed to GADM GID_1. Licence not confirmed, so use numbers only and join by name. Gennaioli et al. 'Growth in Regions' (1,528 regions, 83 countries): no licence found, so avoid.

items.topic: Military: SIPRI, COW and IISS (avoid)
items.finding: SIPRI: commercial use must be authorised and normally needs a royalty; fair use is only non-commercial and under 10% of a dataset. Correlates of War (NMC v6 for 1816-2016, IGO, alliances): the download terms forbid commercial use and distribution to third parties without written permission. IISS Military Balance: a copyrighted annual compilation. Do not transcribe its tables; database rights may apply in the UK and EU. None of the three may be bundled.

items.topic: Military: public-domain US-government sources for 1985
items.finding: US federal works are not copyrighted (17 USC 105), so commercial use and redistribution are allowed; cite them as a courtesy. Sources: DoD 'Soviet Military Power 1985' (4th edition, April 1985; DTIC AD1120503 and the CIA reading room). CIA World Factbook 1985 and 1986 (manpower, defence spending). CIA Handbook of Economic Statistics. ACDA 'World Military Expenditures and Arms Transfers' (annual military spending, armed forces, arms transfers; 1985, 1986 and 1987 volumes exist; ICPSR holds 1973-1983 machine-readable files). Use these to calibrate abstract units (divisions and air wings by personnel and budget) instead of exact equipment counts.

items.topic: Politics: heads of state and government on 1 Jan 1985
items.finding: CIA 'Chiefs of State and Cabinet Members of Foreign Governments', February 1985 (CR CS 85-002; information as of 9 Jan 1985), CIA reading room: public domain, global coverage of heads of state, heads of government and ministers. Use it to check names extracted from Wikidata. The OCR is rough, so manual QA is needed.

items.topic: Politics: Wikidata (CC0) as the machine-readable backbone
items.finding: Structured data in Wikidata's main, Property and Lexeme namespaces is CC0, so it is commercial-safe with no attribution required. Use P35 (head of state), P6 (head of government), P463 (member of) with start and end qualifiers, P122 (form of government), plus Arabic labels and links to NE via wikidataid. Freeze a SPARQL snapshot and review it by hand. Linked Commons files (flags, maps) carry their own licences.

items.topic: Politics: conflicts and regime datasets
items.finding: UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset: CC BY 4.0, may be redistributed with citation; v26.1 covers 1946-2025. Cite Gleditsch et al. 2002, Davies et al. 2025 and the version. Country-dyad-year CSV, under 1 MB. Use it to seed the active conflicts of 1985. V-Dem: CC BY-SA 4.0 (v16, March 2026); share-alike would bind any derived data, so use it only to cross-check. Polity5: copyright of the Center for Systemic Peace, and reproduction or redistribution needs prior written permission, so avoid. Archigos 4.1 (leaders to 2015): no licence stated, so avoid bundling.

items.topic: Politics: blocs and memberships in 1985
items.finding: The EC had 10 members in 1985; Spain and Portugal joined on 1 Jan 1986. Greenland left the EEC on 1 Feb 1985. Morocco left the OAU in Nov 1984. COW IGO v3 cannot be used, so build NATO, Warsaw Pact, NAM, Arab League, GCC, OPEC, Comecon, EEC, ASEAN, OAU and other memberships from Wikidata P463 plus manual checks against the organisations' official histories, and store the evidence URL with each row.

items.topic: Names: GeoNames, CLDR and Arabic sources
items.finding: GeoNames: CC BY 4.0, commercial use allowed with attribution (a link to geonames.org is commonly accepted). It includes Arabic alternate names; dump of about 400 MB (approximate). Unicode CLDR: Unicode License v3; commercial use, modification and sale allowed if the copyright and permission notice is included. It has Arabic names for modern territories. Natural Earth name_ar covers almost all units (measured). Historical 1985 names (USSR, East and West Germany, North and South Yemen, Zaire, Burma, Kampuchea and others) need a hand-written override file reviewed by a native Arabic speaker.

items.topic: Flags
items.finding: lipis/flag-icons is MIT-licensed but has modern flags only. 1985 flags (USSR, GDR, SFRY, YAR, PDRY, Libya 1977, Iraq 1963-91, the Afghan DRA, Zaire, Burma, PR Benin, PR Congo, South Africa 1928-94, colonial Hong Kong, Syria 1980 and others) must be redrawn as in-house SVGs. Wikimedia Commons flag files have per-file licences; many are public domain but this is not universal. National emblems can be protected under Paris Convention Art. 6ter and national symbol laws.

items.topic: Licensing risk: CC 4.0 'no technological measures' clause
items.finding: All CC licences forbid licensees from applying effective technological measures (DRM) that restrict recipients' licensed rights. The 'parallel distribution' exception was rejected for 4.0. Whether App Store FairPlay encryption of a bundle that contains CC BY or CC BY 3.0 IGO-derived data breaches this is untested. Mitigation: prefer public-domain and CC0 sources, and publish the processed CC-BY-derived data files with credits on a public page or repository.

recommendations: Commercial-safe data stack. Geometry: Natural Earth 10m (public domain) as the base, plus a few chosen geoBoundaries files under PD, CC0, CC BY 4.0, CC BY 3.0 IGO or dl-de/by-2-0 (YEM ADM2, NAM ADM2, ZAF ADM3/4, DEU), plus own-work override polygons. Terrain: GMTED2010 or ETOPO 2022 (US gov, public domain), Natural Earth geography regions, rivers and lakes (public domain), ESA WorldCover (CC BY 4.0). Population: UN WPP 2024 (CC BY 3.0 IGO) for country totals and GHS-POP R2023A 1985 epoch (CC BY 4.0) for the province split, with HYDE 3.3 (CC BY 4.0) as a cross-check. Economy: UNSD AMA (UNdata terms) as the canonical 1985 nominal GDP and sector shares; Maddison 2023 (CC BY 4.0) for real PPP; WDI and PWT (CC BY 4.0) and IMF data (attribution) for market economies and public finance; CIA Factbook 1985/86 and the CIA Handbook of Economic Statistics (public domain) for the Soviet bloc; Kummu 1990 grid (CC0) for province productivity. Resources: EIA (PD) and the CIA International Energy Statistical Review (PD); USGS Minerals Yearbook (PD) for steel; FAOSTAT (CC BY 4.0) for food. Military: PD US-government sources (CIA, DoD Soviet Military Power 1985, ACDA WMEAT). Politics: Wikidata (CC0), CIA Chiefs of State Feb 1985 (PD), UCDP/PRIO ACD (CC BY 4.0). Names: Natural Earth name_ar, then Wikidata labels, then CLDR (Unicode-3.0), then GeoNames (CC BY 4.0), then manual 1985 overrides.

Datasets to AVOID: GADM (non-commercial, no redistribution). OSM/ODbL-derived geometry, including 84 of the 199 geoBoundaries ADM1 files (share-alike database risk). geoBoundaries files under CC BY-SA, and gbAuthoritative/UN SALB (non-commercial). CShapes 2.0 (non-commercial). aourednik historical-basemaps (GPL-3.0). All Correlates of War data, including NMC, IGO and alliances (no commercial use or redistribution). SIPRI (commercial use needs a paid permission). IISS Military Balance (copyright). Polity5 (permission needed). V-Dem (CC BY-SA). Archigos and Gennaioli regional data (no licence). Energy Institute Statistical Review (reuse terms not found). Oxford Text Archive Factbook texts (relabelled CC BY-NC-SA). Kaggle and other mirrors (wrong labels; always take data from the original publisher). Wikipedia prose and unchecked Wikimedia Commons files (CC BY-SA, per-file licences).

Use modern Natural Earth admin-1 only as the raw material for an owned 'game province' layer. Merge over-split countries (GBR 232, SVN 193, LVA 119, MLT 68, MKD 84 and others) and split huge units (Siberian regions, Australian and Canadian territories) using a reviewed merge_rules.csv, targeting about 2,500-3,000 provinces. Give each province a permanent ID, never reused and never derived from a source code (NE uses non-ISO codes such as SDS, KOS and PSX), recorded in a committed province_registry.csv, so saves and later scenarios never break.

Represent each scenario as data over the shared province layer: owner, controller, cores and claims per province ID, plus the entity list (flag, Arabic name, government) and events. A 1985 occupation such as south Lebanon, northern Chad, Afghanistan or Cambodia is a controller value, not a geometry edit. Future scenarios (1991, 2000) then need no code changes, which is the 'strong foundation' the user asked for.

Keep the number of hand-made 1985 polygons small and committed as GeoJSON, each with a provenance header (method, public-domain source map, author, date): East/West Berlin, optional Amt Neuhaus, the Yemen YAR/PDRY line (grouped OCHA districts), Walvis Bay (Namibia ADM2), the TBVC bantustans, the Western Sahara 1985 control line, the Aouzou Strip, and optionally the Iraq-Saudi Neutral Zone and Bakassi. Draw only at game resolution (tens to low hundreds of vertices).

Offline pipeline, as Python in the repo under tools/datapipeline, run by one command (e.g. `python -m datapipeline build`) with pinned requirements: (00) fetch.py downloads to a git-ignored raw cache and checks sha256 against sources.yaml (id, publisher, URL, version, SPDX licence, licence URL, attribution text, commercial_ok, sa, nc, retrieved date); (10) geometry.py loads NE, drops unused and GADM-derived columns, applies the 1985 overrides and merge rules, and assigns stable IDs; (11) topology.py builds shared-arc topology, fixes gaps and overlaps, simplifies each shared border once (2-3 detail levels), computes land, strait and sea-zone adjacency and marks river crossings from NE rivers; (12) terrain.py computes per-province elevation, ruggedness and land-cover fractions; (20) population.py sums GHS-POP 1985 per province and scales to WPP or 1985-entity totals, with age structure giving manpower; (21) economy.py takes country GDP and sectors from AMA, Maddison PPP and CIA figures for the Soviet bloc, then sets province shares from population times a productivity index (Kummu 1990, urbanisation, DOSE where licensed); (22) resources.py builds the country oil, gas, coal, steel and food table plus a hand-curated list of resource provinces; (23) military.py builds abstract force templates from PD sources; (24) politics.py builds leaders, regime types, bloc memberships and 1985 conflicts from the Wikidata snapshot, the CIA directory and UCDP, with an evidence column; (25) names_ar.py resolves Arabic names in priority order (overrides, NE, Wikidata, CLDR) and fails on missing or Latin-script names; (30) validate.py with pytest invariants: one owner per province, owners exist, province sums match country totals within 0.5%, symmetric adjacency, no overlaps, plausible value ranges, and every used source on the licence allowlist; (40) pack.py writes quantized int32/int16 delta-encoded coordinates, pre-triangulated meshes (earcut) and struct-of-arrays province tables into versioned binary files plus a schema hash, compressed with LZFSE for Apple's Compression framework; (50) attribution.py generates in-app credits JSON, Settings.bundle Acknowledgements.plist, ATTRIBUTION.md and the verbatim Unicode notice, listing only the sources actually used in that build.

Commit the small generated game data (target under about 10 MB). The iOS build and GitHub Actions then never need Python, GDAL or raw data. A separate CI job reruns the pipeline on cached raw data and fails if the output hash differs. This avoids zip-based hand-offs and builds that ship without their game data.

Lightness budget: do no geometry processing on the device. Ship pre-triangulated meshes with level-of-detail (world zoom from about 50m-equivalent simplification, close zoom from simplified 10m). Draw borders as precomputed line strips in Metal and keep province state as compact arrays. Measured raw NE 10m admin-1 is 1.3M vertices and 40.7 MB, so aim for about 150k-300k vertices at the finest LOD (an estimate to validate on a device).

Fill the economy and military values for socialist states from one canonical series (AMA, scaled with CIA estimates where AMA is thin) and record any alternative values in a notes column. Calibrate gameplay to ratios (GDP per capita, defence-spending share, manpower share) rather than claiming exact 1985 equipment counts.

Publish the processed CC-BY-derived data files and the attribution list on a public page or repository, as a hedge against the CC 'no technological measures' clause under App Store DRM. Keep the paid app's code closed.

Before selling, have an IP lawyer review the licence allowlist, the flag and emblem policy (Paris Convention 6ter), map-sensitivity rules in key App Store regions (Kashmir, Western Sahara, Palestine, Taiwan, Crimea), and the attribution screen. Re-verify every licence on its official page, because this research could not reach most of those pages directly.

Get a native Arabic reviewer to check the Natural Earth and Wikidata Arabic names. Many are machine-sourced from Wikidata, and the transliteration conventions differ between Maghreb and Mashriq usage. Keep a reviewed overrides CSV.
risks: Licence verification limits: direct fetches were blocked during research for gadm.org, naturalearthdata.com, geoboundaries.org, worldbank.org, rug.nl, zenodo.org and others. Licences were confirmed through search summaries of the official pages, GitHub-hosted licence files and the geoBoundaries metadata CSV. Each must be re-verified on the official page before commercial release.

CC BY and CC BY 3.0 IGO forbid licensees from applying DRM that restricts recipients' rights. Distribution through the App Store (FairPlay) is legally untested for this. Prefer PD and CC0 sources and publish the processed data in parallel.
The licence labels in geoBoundaries metadata can be wrong or out of date. Re-check each chosen file (YEM ADM2, ZAF ADM3/4, NAM ADM2, DEU) at its original source (HDX, BKG, Stanford).

Facts are not copyrightable in the US, but the EU and UK sui generis database right can protect substantial extraction from SIPRI, IISS and other compilations. Copying their tables, even manually, carries legal risk.

Natural Earth admin-1 mixes vintages and names (Kenya pre-2013, India post-2019, Crimea coded RUS). Units may change between NE releases. Pin the NE version and key everything by own stable IDs; joining by NE codes risks save breakage and data drift.

1985 economic data for socialist and centrally planned economies is uncertain. CIA, Maddison and UNSD estimates disagree, sometimes by large margins. Any single choice will be disputed by some players, so document it in-game or in the credits.

Hand-digitised polygons (bantustans, the Western Sahara 1985 line, the Berlin sector line, the Aouzou Strip) will be approximations and can be politically sensitive. App Store availability in some countries may be affected by how disputed territories are shown.
Gridded proxies introduce bias: the GHS-POP 1985 epoch is modelled, not a census, and using Kummu 1990 as a 1985 productivity proxy misses 1985-90 changes, including the effects of the Iran-Iraq war.
Wikidata may contain errors or vandalism, and time qualifiers are often missing. A snapshot must be human-reviewed against the CIA February 1985 directory.
Performance: shipping raw NE 10m (1.3M vertices, 40.7 MB GeoJSON) or GeoJSON parsing at launch would break the lightness requirement. Simplification and binary packing are mandatory.

Over-detailed provinces (thousands of tiny municipalities) would hurt the AI's processing time, the user interface on a phone screen, and memory. Under-detailed provinces would hurt the realism of war and economy. The merge rules need playtesting.
Flags and state emblems can be legally protected (Paris Convention 6ter, national symbol laws). Commons flag files have mixed licences.
unverified: Palau's Compact of Free Association effective date (commonly given as 1 Oct 1994; the UN source found gives 1 Nov 1994 for the end of the Trusteeship Council's operation).
Exact day of the Amt Neuhaus transfer to Lower Saxony (late June 1993, commonly 30 Jun 1993).
Exact date of the Libyan withdrawal from the Aouzou Strip (commonly 30 May 1994), and how far Libya and GUNT controlled northern Chad on 1 Jan 1985.
The exact line of the Moroccan berm, and Moroccan-controlled territory in Western Sahara, on 1 Jan 1985.
Golan Heights Law date (14 Dec 1981), Jerusalem Law (30 Jul 1980), Jordan's West Bank disengagement (31 Jul 1988), and the exact IDF positions in Lebanon on 1 Jan 1985.

Egypt's Arab League suspension (1979-1989), Brunei joining ASEAN (7 Jan 1984), New Zealand's ANZUS dispute (1985-86), and other 1985 bloc memberships (NATO 16, Warsaw Pact, Comecon, OPEC 13, GCC 6, NAM, OAU, Arab League).
Whether Maddison 2023 still contains a 'Former USSR' aggregate series (the R package confirms non-ISO codes only for Czechoslovakia and Yugoslavia, for the 2018 version).
Whether WDI lacks 1985 data for the USSR, GDR, Czechoslovakia and Yugoslavia and many CMEA members (well known, not checked here).
Whether the UNSD AMA includes separate GDR and FRG series and separate YAR and PDRY series for 1970-1989.
Which historical entities EIA International Energy Statistics has for 1980-1991 (Former U.S.S.R., East and West Germany, Former Czechoslovakia, Former Yugoslavia).
FAOSTAT area codes for historical entities, and whether FAO's additional terms restrict any commercial use.

Licences of DOSE (believed to be CC BY 4.0), HydroSHEDS, ESA CCI Land Cover, GHS-SMOD, ATOP and REIGN; an explicit licence statement for ETOPO 2022; the Energy Institute Statistical Review reuse terms.
Which ACDA WMEAT volume contains 1985 data (e.g. the 1987 or 1988 volume), and whether ICPSR redistribution terms apply to its machine-readable WMEAT files.
HYDE 3.3 time step around 1985 (whether a 1985 layer exists or only 1980 and 1990).
The exact names of the three GADM-dependent columns in Natural Earth admin-1.

Minor post-1985 border changes, believed negligible at game scale: China-Tajikistan cession (2011), Russia-China islands (1991/2004-2008), India-Bangladesh enclave exchange (2015), Kuwait-Iraq UN demarcation (1993), Eritrea-Yemen Hanish award (1998), Botswana-Namibia Kasikili (1999), Benin-Niger Lete (2005), Israel-Jordan Arava adjustments (1994), Peru-Ecuador settlement (1998), and the Saudi-Yemen (2000) and Oman-Yemen (1992) lines.

List of armed conflicts active in 1985 to seed from UCDP (expected: Iran-Iraq, Afghanistan, Cambodia, Lebanon, Sri Lanka, Ethiopia (Eritrea and Tigray), Sudan, Angola, Mozambique, Western Sahara, Chad, Nicaragua, El Salvador, Guatemala, Peru, Colombia, Philippines, Turkey-PKK, Uganda, Namibia/SWAPO, Punjab, Myanmar, East Timor, Sino-Vietnamese border, Kurdish insurgencies, Somalia, the December 1985 Agacher Strip war).

1985 capitals that differ from today (Bonn and East Berlin, Aden for the PDRY, Lagos before Abuja in 1991, and others) and 1985 country names (Burma, Zaire, Kampuchea and the CGDK UN seat, Swaziland, Western Samoa, Ivory Coast).
Whether App Store FairPlay distribution conflicts with the CC BY 4.0 / CC BY 3.0 IGO technological-measures clause (no authoritative answer found).
The quality of Natural Earth name_ar values (machine-sourced from Wikidata), which needs native review.
